evidence.snippet: Endosomal TLRs play an important role in innate immune response as well as in autoimmune processes. In the therapy of systemic lupus erythematosus, antimalarial drugs chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine, and quinacrine have been used for a long time. Their suppression of endosomal TLR activation has been attributed to the inhibition of endosomal acidification, which is a prerequisite for the activation of these receptors.
evidence.explanation: The study demonstrates antimalarial drugs including hydroxychloroquine inhibit endosomal TLR9 activation.

evidence.snippet: Increased Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR-7) signaling leading to the production of type I interferon (IFN) is an important contributor to human systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

evidence.snippet: One of the most prominent features, shared by the majority of patients with SLE, is a continuous activation of the type I interferon (IFN) system, which manifests as increased serum levels of IFNα and/or an increased expression of type I IFN-induced genes, a so-called type I IFN signature.

paper.title: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus--A Disease with A Dysregulated Type I Interferon System.

evidence.snippet: Type I interferons secreted by plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) play a crucial role in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus by driving the formation of autoantibodies against nuclear debris.

paper.title: Interferon targeted therapies in systemic lupus erythematosus.
